title: Five images of the poem
back: Ashen face (corpse), sprinting trees and children (life), late winter's moon (fading), the triple smile (brave mask).

title: The single sentence, move by move
back: Drive → corpse-like face → looks away at young life → airport, pale moon → childhood fear → smile, smile, smile.

back: The first simile is deliberately shocking: the daughter's sudden recognition that her mother is nearing death. Not illness — age.

back: The winter moon is dim, colourless, misty, at the year's end — the softer second image of ageing and approaching death.

title: The old familiar ache
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A fear carried since childhood, now made real" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><circle cx="90" cy="131.05" r="6.05" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><path d="M81.75,145.10000000000002 Q90,137.10000000000002 98.25,145.10000000000002 L96.93,156.9 L93.3,156.9 L93.96,180 H90.825 L90.33,158.0 H89.67 L89.175,180 H86.04 L86.7,156.9 L83.07,156.9 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/></g><g><circle cx="150" cy="82.1" r="12.1" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="none"/><path d="M133.5,102.19999999999999 Q150,94.19999999999999 166.5,102.19999999999999 L179.7,180 H120.3 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="none"/></g><path d="M100,120 Q120,90 142,110" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="3 3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><text x="230" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">childhood fear</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">A fear carried since childhood, now made real</text></svg>
back: Every child fears losing its mother; the airport parting revives it because the separation it dreaded is visibly coming. 'Familiar' is the key word.

title: The last word, three times
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Line to remember" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><rect x="28" y="36" width="264" height="72" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/><path d="M50,108 L42,122 L64,108 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><text x="160.0" y="77.6" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">smile and smile and smile</text></g><text x="160" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.8" stroke="none">— as she says goodbye</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Line to remember</text></svg>
back: One smile is natural; three are effort. To hide fear, to comfort, to hope. The poem's whole feeling in a repeated word.
